label: How much the next dollar does compared with a charity's past average (per charity)

rows.label: The Humane League: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Animal Charity Evaluators, The Humane League review (2025): room for more funding, cost-effectiveness and organizational health
source.note: Room 0.85: ACE finds THL can spend up to $28.7M a year in 2026-27, $4.4M above its projected $24.3M revenue; reserves above its nine-month target. Use 0.6: over 2,700 cage-free pledges already won and most due by 2024 met; the next dollar goes to the harder rest (companies that haven't implemented, over 40% due in 2025) and to newer regions ACE rates less certain. Run 1.0: ACE finds no decision-relevant concerns; a CEO change in 2025.

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with the past average our models of The Humane League start from: room (is money the constraint) × use (what the next dollar buys compared with the average) × run (how well the organisation is run): 0.85 × 0.6 × 1.0 = 51%, from 30% to 80%.

rows.label: Wild Animal Initiative: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: Animal Charity Evaluators, Wild Animal Initiative review (2025): room for more funding and organizational health
source.note: Room 0.5: ACE finds WAI can spend up to $6.9M a year in 2026-27 (a gap of about $3M), but net assets were over twice its 2024 spending, above its 12-month target. Use 0.6: new money goes to fellows, university hubs, a prize and fundraising staff, some of which ACE rates only moderate. Run 1.05: independent board with public minutes, long-serving director, no major concerns.

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with Wild Animal Initiative's past average: room × use × run = 0.5 × 0.6 × 1.05 = 32%, from 15% to 60%. Low on room: about two years of spending held in reserve.

rows.label: British Heart Foundation: the next dollar compared with its past average

source.title: British Heart Foundation, Trustees' report and accounts, year to 31 March 2025
source.note: Room 0.55: cash and investments £346.4M against a liquidity requirement of £142-176M; new grants fell from £119.3M to £108.4M; no stated funding gap. Use 0.7: no evidence on the marginal grant against the average (neutral). Run 1.0: stable leadership and a new strategy; no external assessment found (neutral).

rows.explainer: How much the next dollar does compared with the British Heart Foundation's past average: room × use × run = 0.55 × 0.7 × 1.0 = 39%, from 20% to 70%. Room is low: reserves well above what its trustees require.
